description: Counterexample fixtures must be verified to reach the specific code path they are named for, not just the named concept
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

In the OpenSIP design-corrections engagement, five times running my control matrix declared a class
covered while the fixture never reached the code site that class names. Latest: a case labelled
`enclosing-container` built a `$ref` container with a sibling `properties` overlay, which is a
second same-path merge and never touched the `inherited` early-collection filter — so it reported
that class as non-discriminating when it in fact discriminates. Root's matrix caught it each time.

**Why:** a fixture named after a concept proves nothing unless the traversal it triggers actually
executes the branch under repair. A green negative can be green because the fixture landed somewhere
else entirely.

**How to apply:** for each counterexample class, verify the fixture reaches the intended site — by
measuring it against the pre-fix image (it must discriminate if the class is affected) or by checking
the sighting/path it produces. When a fixture turns out mislabelled, retain the original probe and
result unmodified and add a superseding note rather than rewriting history. See
[[frozen-bytes-are-not-mine-to-tidy]].

A doubled anchor comment I introduced in `check-identity.py` shipped into frozen v9/v10/v11. I once
"repaired" it, then restored the frozen byte exactly and anchored elsewhere. Same rule applied to
root's stale-pin recording error: root owns it and explicitly asked that work-root pins stay
unchanged, so pin-bearing suites were run in a separate disposable sandbox instead.

**Why:** a tidy-up inside a delta puts an unrequested change into the other party's record, and any
delta wider than the stated ownership is not reviewable as the correction it claims to be.

**How to apply:** keep the delta to exactly the owned paths; prove it with a whole-tree hash sweep
against the frozen image. Disclose known cosmetic defects as mine with disposition left to root
rather than fixing them. See [[fixture-must-hit-the-code-site]].
